description: Allowlist of EXPECTED VM-vs-JIT divergences, pinned by corpus id (WF-0B). A non-MATCH on a listed id is reported but does not fail the run; a MATCH on a listed id is flagged for removal. Add entries ONLY with an audit/issue citation — this file must never become a dumping ground that greens a red gate.

knownClasses.hof-return-kind-raw-bits: WF-0B baseline 2026-07-05 (repro: acceptance program finding_s1_unknown_hof_return_kind_confusion): a higher-order-function return whose kind is unproven is printed as a raw f64 bit pattern under jit (vm '6.0' vs jit '4618441417868443648'), both exit 0. RECLASSIFIED 2026-07-05 (WF-1A -> WF-3A type-system-edges + let-generalization): NOT a JIT return-kind-table drift. Root: `fn apply(f, x) { f(x) }` has an UNPROVABLE return type (untyped param `f`), so `let bad: int = apply(ret_num, 3.0)` is admitted by the checker where `r` is number-valued — the `: int` annotation unifies against an unresolved type var and the JIT then stamps the slot Int64 and prints the f64 payload's bits. Sound fix is type-system-side: HOF return-kind inference / HM let-generalization so `apply` gets a generic return `R` (= number here), after which `let bad: int = <number>` is a D2 numeric-conversion compile error (no implicit number->int). Deeper than a kind stamp; owned by WF-3A. Shows up as DIVERGED, deterministic.
knownClasses.compile-blowup-timeout: Audit 2026-07-04 'Parser exponential blowup' (CONFIRMED, shape.pest:1099): compile phase alone exceeds the 10s/mode harness budget in BOTH modes; with a 60s budget the program produces the identical compile error in both modes (would be MATCH). Harness-budget artifact of a known compiler-performance bug (WF-0C), not a VM/JIT divergence. Entry-less on fast hosts where ACC__pattern-matching__large completes within budget (classifies MATCH).
knownClasses.comptime-typedstring-verify-nondetermini: WF-1A-followup 2026-07-05 (repro: ACC__comptime__pb3.shape — a `comptime fn names() -> Array<string>` that push()es string literals, invoked from `comptime { names() }`). PRE-EXISTING, NONDETERMINISTIC, and INDEPENDENT of the jit-fallback-engine-isolation fix. The comptime typed-string-array path emits V2 typed opcodes (NewTypedArrayString / TypedArrayPushString) WITHOUT a FrameDescriptor, so BOTH modes fail V2 bytecode verification identically ('has no FrameDescriptor', 3 violations) and then execute the mis-verified bytecode into undefined behaviour whose crash mode FLAPS across runs: sometimes a rust_decimal parse panic (exit 101), sometimes 'Not implemented: SURFACE: GetProp on Ptr(Decimal) not yet kinded' (exit 1). PROVEN pre-existing via a base-vs-patched determinism check 2026-07-05: on the UNPATCHED base binary (fbfd050e) the program flakes jit={101,1,101,101,1} with vm consistently 101 (one vm=1 sample on the patched binary too); on the patched binary it flakes identically jit={1,101,101,101,1,101}. The WF-1A baseline happened to sample the both-101 MATCH side; a later run samples the vm=101/jit=1 DIVERGED side. Root cause is a comptime typed-string-array FrameDescriptor gap (comptime-marshal territory), NOT a VM/JIT or engine-isolation divergence — owned by a separate comptime follow-up. Pinned so the flake does not spuriously red/green the gate; a MATCH sample is EXPECTED here (do NOT auto-remove on a single now-matching sample).

notes: WF-1A closed 4 of the 6 original classes (2026-07-05): jit-double-execution (item 1, program.rs compile-stage deopt), i64-overflow-wrap (item 2, compile_int64_checked_arith + JIT_SIGNAL_INT_OVERFLOW), annotation-hooks-dropped (item 3, functions.rs mir_data suppression for wrapped fns), and hashmap-filter-garbage (item 4, function_calls.rs receiver_is_array gate on the *Indexed rewrite). Their SYN__/ACC__ repro programs stay in the corpus as regression MATCH cases — the entries were removed here because a MATCH on a listed id is a stale-pin failure. The two remaining classes were RECLASSIFIED (root deeper than WF-1A JIT-table alignment) and routed to WF-3A (hof-return-kind, 1 entry) and a WF-1A-followup engine-isolation lane (object-merge, now 4 entries). Fixing item 4 UNMASKED a 4th object-merge instance (ACC__collections__large): the program used to fail identically in both modes at its arity-2 HashMap.filter and now progresses far enough to hit the pre-existing dirty-engine-fallback merge bug under JIT (VM is now correct). If a future run turns a remaining known-red entry into MATCH, remove it here. The 3 registry_cross_check-only drifts (Array<int>.mean, HashMap.iter, HashMap.get) are pinned/retired in crates/shape-jit/src/mir_compiler/types.rs, not here (they have no corpus program). RESOLVED 2026-07-05 (WF-1A-followup jit-fallback-engine-isolation): the jit-object-merge-field-add class (4 entries: ACC__objects-arrays__small, ACC__operators__small, ACC__operators__large, ACC__collections__large) is fixed and its entries removed. Root cause was the [jit-fallback] path recompiling `program` on the inspection-compile-mutated engine (advanced schema_registry.next_id), shifting ambient-domain merged/named SchemaIds while compiler-local inline-object ids reset → collision (MakeFieldRef field_idx out of bounds). Fix: extracted execute_compiled from execute_program (crates/shape-vm/src/execution.rs) and the fallback (crates/shape-jit/src/executor.rs) now runs the ALREADY-BUILT inspection bytecode instead of a second compile — no counter re-advance, byte-identical to --mode vm. Verified 2026-07-05 (WF-1A-followup finisher): all 4 object-merge ids now DETERMINISTICALLY MATCH (stdout+exit+program-stderr identical to --mode vm across repeated runs). The finisher's fresh 467-program corpus re-run surfaced ONE additional non-MATCH — ACC__comptime__pb3.shape — which a base-vs-patched determinism check PROVED is a PRE-EXISTING nondeterministic flake (flaps exit 101/1 in both modes on the UNPATCHED base binary fbfd050e), NOT a shared-deopt-path regression from this fix; it is now pinned above as comptime-typedstring-verify-nondeterministic (root: comptime typed-string-array FrameDescriptor gap, comptime follow-up). With that pin the gate is green (no unexpected non-MATCH from this change).
